title: Seat a keyed coupling and prove drive transfer
context: Robot drive maintenance requires a coupling to transmit rotation after assembly. This task checks both seating over unequal drive dogs and actual motion of the lower rotor. Placing the coupling on top without transferring rotation cannot earn full credit.
scoring: Score zero if the coupling ever goes more than 4 mm below the table. A seated coupling must have its centre within 4 mm on each axis of x 280 mm and y negative 30 mm and z 811.5 mm. Tilt must be below 5 degrees. Coupling yaw relative to the measured lower rotor angle must be below 5 degrees. Seating earns 0.5. Engagement is recorded only when seating occurs while the lower rotor is within 5 degrees of zero. After engagement the rotor must turn beyond 80 degrees and remain below 100 degrees while the coupling stays seated. Translation must be below 8 mm per second and rotation below 0.1 radians per second. This earns 0.75. Both measured grippers open beyond 35 mm raises this to 1.0. Full success must hold for 2 seconds. A previously engaged coupling that is no longer seated earns 0.25. All other outcomes score zero.
fidelity: The fixture is fixed to the table. The lower rotor has a passive revolute joint with angular damping 0.005 and no drive force. The unequal rigid dogs enter actual pockets in the upper coupling. Contact transmits rotation. Every part is printed PA12 polymer. This is an unpowered assembly test rather than a precision servo drive. Motor power and wear are not modelled.
instruction: Hold the lower drive hub still by its long lever. Seat the orange coupling over both unequal drive dogs. Release the lower lever and turn the orange coupling through 90 degrees so the lower hub turns with it. Release both grippers. Leave the coupling seated. All equipment is unpowered.
setup: Use the bimanual YAM station with the tabletop at z 747.5 mm. x points forward. y points left. z points up. Every part is printed PA12 polymer. scene_inventory.json lists every object and every solid with exact dimensions and initial positions in metres and masses in kilograms. Object positions use the world frame. Solid positions use their body frame. Joint anchors and limits are listed with the articulated object. The setup image shows this fixed layout. All joint positions start at zero.
run_limit: 600 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 30 seconds of control time.
reset_notes: Restore every object to the starting pose in scene_inventory.json and every joint to zero. Nothing is consumed. Use one epoch with seed 0 and object_jitter=0.
scores: Both uploaded videos show the same scripted demo with score 1.0. No model score is claimed.
